flagged.title: Quantitative Chemistry: Moles, Mass and Yield
flagged.reason: The video defines atom economy using total Mr of all products as the denominator instead of all reactants, which risks marks in GCSE definition questions.

mark_affecting.quote: Atom economy equals the relative formula mass, the Mr, of your useful products divided by the total Mr of all products times 100.

flagged.title: Reactivity, Metal Extraction and Alloys
flagged.reason: The video incorrectly states the resulting iron(II) sulfate solution becomes colorless rather than pale green, which loses an exam observation mark.

mark_affecting.quote: The solution changes from that bright blue to a completely colorless iron(II) sulfate

flagged.title: Acids, pH and Making Salts
flagged.reason: The video explicitly claims that the core practical preparation of copper sulfate has an independent variable (the amount of acid used) and uses a thermometer, which teaches incorrect scientific methodology and would lose marks in an exam.

mark_affecting.quote: Remember that the independent variable is the amount of acid used, and if you're using a water bath and a thermometer, just remember the thermometer only measures the temperature, it's the water bath that actually controls it.
